chapter_theme: Two songs at Thiruverkadu (திருவேற்காடு): the poet confesses the women's eyes, breasts and waist that keep him taking bodies, and his lust as a great sinner, and asks when the round of births will end and whether Murugan will look on him, join him to the devotees and give him one word, as he rescued Nakkirar.

680.reading: Through eyes dark as poison that wage war, breasts and a slender waist, the poet, without support, takes body after body, and asks Murugan to say when that time will end. The praise names Murugan the child of the milk-fragrant mother, the lord of Vayalur, nephew of Vishnu, with the hunter girl and the heavenly maiden on either side, giver of the Veda and of nada, at Velangadu.
680.nuance: அநேகம் காயம் ... காலம் தான் ஒழிவது ஏது: desire is tied directly to rebirth, the many bodies. The second half of the plea (சாலந்தாழ்வுறு மால ஏலங்கோர் பிடியாய) is hard to divide. வேலங்காடு is Verkadu.

681.reading: Infatuated with women of dark hair, spear eyes, milk-sweet speech, thread waists and tender-coconut breasts, the poet calls himself a lustful great sinner and asks: will Murugan not look on him by grace, not join him to his devotees, not sharpen his grace; and as he once rescued Keeran, who excelled on the old sea-girt earth through the poets' words, will he not give him one word. The praise names Murugan as the one whose angry word destroyed the sects built on false causes, the Siva-faith and the yoga of the great, the life of devotees, the son of Vedapurisvara at Thiruverkadu, and the bridegroom of Indra's daughter.
681.nuance: The plea is a run of questions ending in அலையோ (பார்ப்பாய் அலையோ, சேர்ப்பாய் அலையோ, கூர்ப்பாய் அலையோ). கீரரை ஆர்ப்பாய்: Nakkirar, whom tradition says Murugan freed from captivity, is the precedent for the poet's request for one word (ஒர் சொல்). The praise lines on sects (மத ஏற்பாடிகளே அழிவே உற) are uncertain in division.
